title: Post-Market Clinical-Follow-Up Study of BonOs® R NF Genta, OSARTIS GmbH
summary: The study is planned as a clinical follow-up study of a surgical knee or hip surgery. The tested medical device BonOs® R NF Genta is a fast-curing polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) bone cement, which is already certified as a medical device for use in joint surgery. BonOs® R NF Genta contains the antibiotic gentamicin sulfate, which protects the implant and surrounding tissue from infection with bacteria that can be treated with this antibiotic. The mechanical properties of BonOs® R NF Genta ensure a reliable anchoring of the prosthesis in the bone. PMMA bone cements for joint replacement have been used for 50 years, and the composition of BonOs® R NF Genta is based on the experience gained. Usage of BonOs® R NF Genta relies on the knowledge of established procedures in the operating room and is mixed and used in a familiar manner. In addition, BonOs® R NF Genta also contains zirconium dioxide. Thus, doctors can check the distribution of the cement in the bone and around the implant in X-ray images assuring optimal results of the operation. The purpose of this study is to collect data as a clinical follow-up to better assess scientifically how safe the product is to use. For 5 years, it will be observed how well patients have tolerated the bone cement and whether they report any side effects. On the one hand, it is documented whether known side effects have occurred in the patients. On the other hand, it is also observed whether they may report new side effects that were not yet known.
conditions: Surgical Joint Replacement: Primary complete or partial / unicompartmental knee arthroplasty or hip arthroplasty.

interventions.name: Data of the study will be collected as part of the scheduled appointments before and after artificial knee or hip replacement surgery, respectively. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Male or female aged between 18 – 85 years (on the day of
screening )
2) Patient requires primary total or partial/unicompartmental knee ar-throplasty or hip arthroplasty
3) Planned routine radiographs at 12 ± 2 months after the intervention
4) Patient has signed written Informed Consent
5) Subjects able and willing to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all study procedures
Exclusion criteria:
1) Bilateral surgical intervention
2) Severe generalized disease resulting in a life expectancy shorter than 12 months
3) Pregnant or breast-feeding women (urine pregnancy test) 
4) Women of childbearing potential without effective contraception
5) Alcohol- or drug abuse (clinical manifestation)
6) Subjects with psychiatric disorders influencing their judgement or autonomy
7) Inability or unwillingness to understand or comply with required study procedures
8) Subjects who are not suitable for the study based on the principal investigator’s evaluation
9) Muscle wasting or neuromuscular compromise in the affected limb renders the procedure unjustifiable.
10) Known hypersensitivity to any of its constituents
11) Patients with severe renal failure
